stated: Reform UK will legislate to ban ULEZ, Clean Air Zones, and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods, scrap 20 MPH zones (except where safety is critical), and remove bans on petrol and diesel cars and legal requirements for manufacturers to sell electric cars.

source.quote: Stop the War on Drivers Legislate to ban ULEZ Clean Air Zones and Low Traffic Neighbourhoods. Scrapping Net Zero means no more bans on petrol and diesel cars and no legal requirements for manufacturers to sell electric cars. We will keep the speed limit low where safety is critical. Otherwise, 20 MPH zones will be scrapped.

bearing_set.reason: Banning ULEZ/Clean Air Zones and removing EV mandates/petrol-diesel phase-out directly affects air quality and the UK's emissions trajectory — a non-negligible verdict is unavoidable.
Scrapping 20 MPH zones (with only narrow safety exceptions) would plausibly affect road casualty rates, which sits squarely within the safety/streets indicator of O5.

Removing ULEZ and Clean Air Zone charges reduces a direct recurring cost on lower-income drivers of older, non-compliant vehicles, and removing EV sales mandates affects the pace and price pressure of the vehicle market — real disposable-income effect for a material subset of households.

Abolishing charges, LTNs, 20 mph mandates, and manufacturer EV requirements withdraws state coercion over how and what people drive — a direct improvement on personal liberty and freedom from mandates.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O6 (clear worsening mechanism on air quality and emissions), O10 (clear liberty-improving mechanism via deregulation of mandates and charges), and O2 (real cost relief for households facing daily ULEZ/CAZ charges). O14 (inequality) was considered — ULEZ is somewhat regressive — but that distributional effect is adequately captured under O2 without requiring a separate O14 verdict. O5 was considered for 20mph zone removal but road-traffic safety is not within O5's indicator scope (crime, justice, national security).
